Claim: The new Republican tax law provides 'at least a $1.3 trillion tax break for corporations.'
Ended: Jan 12, 2018 (FactCheck.org: misleading; net business cut ~$654B)
Deception_Form: cherry-picked line item / ignoring offsetting tax increases
Notes: FactCheck.org: Pelosi cited JCT corporate-rate cut (~$1.35T) but ignored other business provisions; net business tax cut ~$654B. Rating: misleading.

Claim: Repealing the ACA individual mandate in the GOP tax bill would 'boot' 13 million people from the health insurance rolls.
Ended: Nov 17, 2017 (FactCheck.org: Distorts the Facts)
Deception_Form: voluntary disenrollment framed as kicking people off
Notes: CBO/JCT estimated 13M fewer insured by 2025–27 if mandate penalty repealed; FactCheck: many would drop voluntarily, not be 'booted.'

Claim: Republicans want to pay for tax cuts for the wealthy by 'taking health care away from 13 million Americans.'
Ended: Nov 17, 2017 (FactCheck.org Distorts the Facts on same talking point)
Deception_Form: CBO uninsured estimate reframed as forced loss of coverage
Notes: Same CBO 13M figure; FactCheck: not equivalent to taking coverage away from 13M.

Claim: The GOP health/tax plan would 'knock 13 million people off health care.'
Ended: Nov 17, 2017 (FactCheck.org Distorts the Facts)
Deception_Form: CBO coverage estimate framed as forced removal
Notes: FactCheck.org grouped Warren with Schumer/Durbin on the inaccurate 'knock off' framing of CBO mandate estimates.

Claim: The GOP tax plan 'Sabotages the health care of 13 MILLION Americans.'
Ended: Nov 29, 2017 (PolitiFact Half True: leaves out voluntary exits)
Deception_Form: omits that most of the 13M would leave coverage voluntarily
Notes: PolitiFact Half True: 'partially accurate but leaves out important details or takes things out of context'; 'Sabotaged' doesn't fit for ~2/3 voluntary leavers (RAND).

Claim: Trump and Republicans 'passed a tax bill that gave 80 percent of its benefits to the top 1 percent.'
Ended: Jan 16, 2018 (PolitiFact Half True: cherry-picks 2027)
Deception_Form: cherry-picking post-sunset year (2027) as if typical
Notes: TPC: top 1% got ~20.5% of benefits in 2018 and ~25% in 2025; ~83% only in 2027 after middle-class provisions expire. PF: leaves out important details.

Claim: With the Trump tax law, '70 percent of the benefits went to the wealthiest 1 percent.'
Ended: Mar 5, 2019 (PolitiFact Half True)
Deception_Form: cherry-picking 2027 distribution
Notes: PolitiFact Half True: partially accurate but leaves out important information; through 2025 top 1% share ~20–25%.

Claim: Under the Republican tax law, 'the rich folks got $1.5 trillion.'
Ended: Jan 9, 2019 (PolitiFact Half True: overstates share for the rich)
Deception_Form: conflates total deficit cost with amount going only to the rich
Notes: JCT ~$1.5T net cost; top ~10% (~$200k+) got about half (~$750B–$1T), not all $1.5T. PF: exaggerated gains for the well-to-do.

Claim: Between the first and second quarters of 2018 — after the tax cuts were enacted — real wages fell by 1.8 percent.
Ended: Aug 1, 2018 (PolitiFact Mostly False)
Who_Pushed_It: Nancy Pelosi / TeamPelosi (also DGA, Fight for $15)
Deception_Form: outlier private index treated as official wage crash
Notes: PayScale Index outlier; BLS median usual weekly real earnings rose slightly Q1→Q2 2018. PF Mostly False.

Claim: Trump's FY2020 budget 'slashes investments in health care to pay for tax cuts to billionaires.'
Ended: Mar 20, 2019 (PolitiFact Half True: no direct pay-for link; 'billionaires' overstated)
Deception_Form: indirect budget pressure framed as earmarked pay-for for billionaires
Notes: PF Half True: health cuts real on Medicaid side; no direct link to TCJA; all income groups got cuts in 2019 on average.

Claim: Under Trump, 'the cost of living is going up, but paychecks aren't keeping up.'
Ended: Jan 29, 2019 (FactCheck.org: wages had risen in real terms)
Deception_Form: contradicted by then-current BLS real earnings data
Notes: FactCheck: real average weekly earnings for production/nonsupervisory workers up ~2.5% since Trump took office; paychecks had kept up with inflation.

Claim: The Trump administration's response was to 'give away a trillion dollars to the biggest corporations in this country.'
Ended: Jan 29, 2019 (FactCheck.org: net business cut ~$654B, not $1T)
Deception_Form: gross corporate-rate cut treated as net giveaway
Notes: Campaign confirmed she meant corporate-rate cut; JCT net business tax reduction ~$653.8B. FactCheck: exaggerated / cherry-picked.

Claim: After exploding the deficit with the GOP tax scam, Trump is trying to 'ransack Medicare, Medicaid and the health care of seniors.'
Ended: Mar 22, 2019 (FactCheck.org: Spins the Facts on Medicare 'slash/ransack')
Deception_Form: provider payment slowdowns framed as ransacking beneficiary Medicare
Notes: FactCheck Spins the Facts: Medicaid cuts significant; Medicare net ~$515–575B mostly provider payment changes resembling Obama-era proposals, not direct beneficiary 'ransack.'

Claim: House Republicans' 'big, beautiful bill' will take Medicaid & health insurance away from 13.7 million Americans.
Ended: May 16, 2025 (PolitiFact Half True; FactCheck.org: Democrats exaggerate)
Deception_Form: bundles bill score with separate credit-expiration baseline
Notes: CBO: bill alone ≥8.6M uninsured by 2034; 13.7M adds 4.2M from enhanced PTC expiration (current law) + marketplace rule effects. PF: ignores information / out of context.

Claim: The GOP Energy & Commerce reconciliation agenda will 'kick at least 13.7 million people off of health care coverage according to the CBO.'
Ended: May 16, 2025 (FactCheck.org: Democrats Exaggerate)
Deception_Form: attributes combined policy package solely to the bill
Notes: FactCheck: CBO said legislation alone ≥8.6M; 13.7M includes PTC expiration not solely the bill.

Claim: 13.7 million Americans will be cut off from their health care and made completely uninsurable by the Republican bill.
Ended: May 16, 2025 (FactCheck.org Exaggerate)
Deception_Form: inflates bill-only CBO figure; adds 'completely uninsurable'
Notes: Same CBO math: bill ≥8.6M; 13.7M is multi-action total Democrats requested.

Claim: At least 14 million Americans would be 'ripped off of their health insurance' under the House Republican Medicaid proposal.
Ended: May 16, 2025 (FactCheck.org: CBO did not say nearly 14M from the proposal alone)
Deception_Form: rounds up and attributes multi-action total to the bill
Notes: FactCheck explicitly notes Schumer's ~14M claim exceeded what CBO attributed to the legislative proposal alone (≥8.6M).

Claim: Trump 'just denied North Carolina’s request for FEMA relief from Hurricane Helene,' calling it unwarranted (implying relief ended).
Ended: Apr 24, 2025 (PolitiFact Half True: missing context—90% cost share continues)
Deception_Form: denial of 100% cost-share extension framed as denying FEMA relief
Notes: FEMA denied extending 100% federal cost share; continued 90% (vs normal 75%). PF: leaves out important detail.

Claim: The 2017 GOP 'tax scam' 'gave 83% of the benefits to the top 1%' (stated as what the law did, without the 2027 sunset caveat).
Ended: Mar 16, 2021 (PolitiFact Half True: cherry-picked 2027)
Deception_Form: 2027 expiry-year share presented as the law's overall effect
Notes: PF Half True: incomplete talking point; through 2025 top 1% share ~20–25%. WaPo Kessler also documented Jeffries/Biden repeating the zombie 83% claim.

Claim: Biden clipped Trump as proposing cuts to Social Security and Medicare from a CNBC line about 'cutting' entitlements (omitting waste/fraud context and later denials).
Ended: Mar 15, 2024 (FactCheck.org: full CNBC answer + Breitbart clarification)
Deception_Form: selective clip truncating qualifying language
Notes: FactCheck: Trump said cutting and also theft/bad management; later said he would never hurt SS/Medicare benefits. Room for disagreement, but Biden's 'end of quote' framing cut short.

Claim: Trump is 'threatening to slash Medicare' / 'wants to cut Social Security and Medicare' (as stated at DNC 2024 without his repeated no-cut pledges).
Ended: Aug 20, 2024 (FactCheck.org: Trump has consistently said he will not cut either)
Who_Pushed_It: Wisconsin Lt. Gov. Sara Rodriguez; President Joe Biden
Deception_Form: past budget proposals / CNBC clip treated as current intent to cut benefits
Notes: FactCheck DNC night 1: Trump consistently said he will not cut SS/Medicare benefits; budgets targeted waste/disability/provider ideas. Distinct from already-covered 'gut SS/Medicare' absolute falsehoods.

Claim: Trump 'lost millions of jobs in America' (as a presidency scorecard without pandemic context).
Ended: Aug 20, 2024 (FactCheck.org: ignores COVID job-loss cause)
Deception_Form: pandemic employment collapse attributed as Trump job-loss record
Notes: BLS: +6.7M jobs first 37 months; −21.9M Mar–Apr 2020 COVID; −2.7M net end of term. FactCheck: claim ignores the pandemic reason.

Claim: Billionaires pay an average federal tax rate of 8.2% (presented as the ordinary tax-system rate).
Began: Aug 19, 2024 (Biden DNC; also prior WH talking point)
Ended: Aug 20, 2024 (FactCheck.org: misleading White House calc with unrealized gains)
Deception_Form: unrealized capital gains counted as income in bespoke rate
Notes: White House 2021 analysis counting unrealized gains; FactCheck: not the average rate in the current tax system; top earners pay higher rates on realized income.

Claim: Trump 'created the largest debt any president had in four years with his $2 trillion tax cut for the wealthy' (as if Trump alone caused all added debt via that cut).
Ended: Aug 20, 2024 (FactCheck.org: incomplete; pre-existing debt path + Congress + COVID)
Deception_Form: assigns all term debt increase to one tax cut and one person
Notes: Debt rose ~$7.8T under Trump; CBO Jan 2017 already projected large rises; TCJA needed Congress; COVID spending major. FactCheck: Trump alone not responsible for all debt added.

Claim: Reconciliation was used in 2017 to pass the GOP tax scam where '83 percent of the benefits went to the wealthiest 1 percent' (Jeffries zombie claim).
Began: Jul 2021 (Jeffries remarks; WaPo Fact Checker column Jul 20, 2021)
Ended: Jul 20, 2021 (WaPo documents as zombie/misleading 83% claim)
Deception_Form: cherry-picking 2027 TPC share
Notes: WaPo Kessler: 83% is 2027 figure after sunsets; 2018 top 1% share 20.5%. Same incomplete talking point PolitiFact rated Half True for Pelosi/DNC. Distinct speaker from Pelosi 2021 case.

Claim: Trump said he wants to be a dictator on 'Day 1' (presented without the border/drill jest context).
Ended: Aug 20, 2024 (FactCheck.org: full Hannity exchange + later 'joking' clarification)
Deception_Form: joke/qualified Day-1 remark framed as open dictatorship pledge
Notes: Hannity town hall: 'except for Day 1' then specified closing border and drilling; later said joking. FactCheck covers the misleading citation. Dedup: 'dictator' alone was HIT but 'Day 1' was NEW.

Claim: Trump's budget 'cuts $845 billion, almost a trillion dollar cut in Medicare.'
Ended: Mar 26, 2019 (PolitiFact Mostly False)
Deception_Form: gross baseline reduction inflated to 'almost a trillion' beneficiary cut
Notes: PF Mostly False: after relocating DSH/GME, net closer to $515–595B; mostly provider payment slowdowns; spending still rises year to year. Distinct stronger rating than FactCheck 'Spins' on similar Dem talking points.

Claim: 'In America, there is a father who is holding down two jobs and paying more taxes than the richest 400 families in America' (post-TCJA justice framing).
Ended: Nov 21, 2019 (PolitiFact Mostly False)
Deception_Form: tax rates study misstated as dollars of taxes paid
Notes: Saez-Zucman rate comparison; Harris said paying more taxes (dollars). PF Mostly False. Used to attack post-2017 Trump tax settlement for the rich.

Claim: Donald Trump 'issued a Muslim ban as president' (implying a ban on all Muslims).
Ended: Aug 21, 2024 (FactCheck.org: misleading; EOs covered selected countries, not all Muslims)
Deception_Form: country-list travel restrictions labeled as total Muslim ban
Notes: FactCheck: 2017 EOs/proclamation restricted nationals of listed countries (not all Muslims); Pew: first EO would have affected ~12% of world Muslims. Primary = EO text.

Claim: Trump 'wrote' Project 2025.
Ended: Aug 22, 2024 (FactCheck.org: false; Heritage document; Trump disavowed)
Deception_Form: authorship falsehood
Notes: FactCheck: Trump did not write Project 2025; Heritage Mandate for Leadership; Trump said it doesn't speak for him. Proven false authorship claim. Primary points to Heritage Project 2025 authorship/home (not Trump).

Claim: Trump 'wants the middle class to pay the price for another huge tax cut that would mostly help him and his rich friends.'
Ended: Aug 21, 2024 (FactCheck.org: proposed extensions/cuts benefit all income levels on average)
Deception_Form: distributional overstatement of proposed tax agenda
Notes: FactCheck: Trump proposals (extend TCJA individual cuts, no tax on tips/SS) benefit taxpayers across incomes; TPC: extending TCJA individuals ~45% of benefits to $450k+, not 'mostly' him and rich friends alone.

Claim: The only economic promise Trump kept was to 'cut taxes for the rich' (implying no broader tax cuts).
Ended: Aug 22, 2024 (FactCheck.org: TPC said TCJA reduced taxes on average for all income groups)
Deception_Form: erases across-the-board average tax cuts
Notes: FactCheck cites TPC: TCJA would reduce taxes on average for all income groups in 2018 and 2025. Distinct from Fox 'billionaire-only' batch5 item—this is Buttigieg DNC line. 'cut taxes for the rich' phrase HIT in corpus may be different claim—verify.
